topic: A clearance application that needed three follow-ups, two visits, and four WhatsApp messages — for one client
format: Walk through the exact day-in-the-life of a Sanad office manager handling 20+ client companies with no case tracking system — every painful step in sequence
post:
Three follow-ups. Two office visits. Four WhatsApp messages.

That's what it took to close one clearance application for one client last week.

And while that was happening, 19 other companies were waiting on their own requests — work permits, visa renewals, MOL filings — all of it living in a thread buried somewhere in your phone.

This is what a real day looks like.

Morning: Client 7 sends a screenshot asking about a permit submitted three weeks ago. You search three separate chats to find the reference number.

Midday: Client 12 calls. Their employee's residency expires in 11 days. You had no idea.

Evening: you're reconciling invoices by hand because nothing connects the service to the payment.

You're not failing. You're doing solid work inside a system that was never designed to hold this much.
